units.translation: where L. Dindorf corrected the faulty accent λατρῶν [of hired servants] in the Thesaurus vol. 5 p. 132. Aristophanes of Byzantium in Eustathius p. 1246, 9 and other grammarians cited in the Thesaurus explain it as μισθός [wages]. Properly it was no doubt said of the pay given to a slave.
And there is a dwelling, a double one: one part Pelasgus, the other the city gives, to live without hired servants.

In Hesychius it is paroxytone λάχη [allotments]: λῆξις, ἀποκλήρωσις [allotment, assignment by lot]. The oxytone form agrees with Herodian's rule in Arcadius p. 115, 19. Moreover, the scholiast's interpretation αἱ σκαφαί [the digging] is foolish, as in Homer Od. 24, 241 "φυτὸν ἀμφελάχαινεν [he dug around the plant]."

It is constructed with the accusative or with the infinitive, or with the accusative and infinitive, with the dative of the person to whom something is said either added or omitted. Examples of this common usage arranged according to the order of the plays are these.
